title: Ops signal handoff & staffing heuristics — quick reference
content:
Purpose:
A compact day-of-ops quick reference for signal handoffs, staffing heuristics, and comm templates. Lightweight companion to the full runbook; put in people pockets and Slack thread.

Summary notes (TL;DR):
- Primary watch: latency p99, error-rate (5xx), queue depth on model router.
- Gate thresholds (pre-agreed): p99 latency > 1200ms sustained 5m OR 5xx spike > 1.5x baseline -> pause rollout.
- Minimum staffing: 2 infra ops, 1 serving-runtime, 1 product owner (on-call), 1 liaison for customer comms for first 4 hours.

8-hour rollout day calendar (example):
- T-72h: smoke test branch and verify telemetry dashboards (owner: serving-runtime).
- T-24h: announce canary windows to #release-ops and post link to checklist (owner: release lead).
- T-2h: preflight: token burn, KV cache warm, routing table snapshot.
- T-30m: go/no-go standup (15m): confirm staffing, last-minute tickets clear.
- T:00: start phased traffic shift: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% (pause 10m inspection between steps).
- T+4h: retrospective snapshot, early customer notes if needed.

Day-of checklist (quick ticks):
- Preflight: infra autoscaler set to lock; dedicated burst capacity enabled.
- Observability: open p99/latency, 5xx, request-rate, model-mismatch (eval) dashboards.
- Canary: deploy variant tag vX.Y.canary; verify health endpoints across regions.
- Traffic ramp: manual increments by release conductor; automated guardrails active.
- Fallback ready: compatible model variant pre-warmed and pinned to routing rule.

Signal handoff template (Slack):
- Channel: #release-ops
- Message skeleton: [ROLLOUT START] service X | canary vX.Y | step 1 -> 5% | watchers: @maya @liam @pri | links: <dashboards> <PR> <jira>
- Handoff: on-call -> steady-state steward. Use: "handoff: READY / WATCHING / ESCALATE" tags.

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Latency p99 > 1200ms for 5 continuous minutes AND error-rate > 1.5x baseline -> immediate rollback to previous routing snapshot.
- Model quality regression confirmed by eval set (regen mismatch > 8% for important prompts) -> rollback to model vA.B.

Comms snippets (customer-facing quick blurb):
- If minor: "We're rolling a small update to inference routing for better latency; you may see brief fluctuations as traffic rebalances. We're monitoring closely."
- If rollback: "We observed increased errors and rolled back to ensure stability. No customer data was affected. Follow-up notes TBD."

Operational heuristics (staffing & shifts):
- Peak watch: first 60-90 minutes after each ramp step. Rotate a "sampler" (30m) to watch telemetrics and run smoke sample prompts.
- Escalation ladder: steward -> serving-runtime lead -> SRE bridge -> CTO-pepline if customer-impacting after 20m.
- Quiet-window rule: avoid unrelated merges + non-critical infra changes for 4h post 100% rollout.

Post-rollout items (first 24h):
- 1h: short retro in #release-ops with signal summary.
- 4h: snapshot telemetry and save timestamped dashboards.
- 24h: final release notes published to Confluence + update changelog.

Release notes draft (skeleton):
- Title: "vX.Y — inference routing optimization rollout (canary)"
- Summary: "Incremental rollout of routing perf improvements (kernel selection, cache prewarm). No API changes."
- Impact: "Improved tail latency expected for long-context requests; no breaking changes."
- Known issues: "Occasional 502s observed in canary region us-west-2 during early ramp (mitigated)."
- Rollback window: "Immediate rollback criteria defined; actioned once during canary and finalized."

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Do we want automated ramp if telemetry is green for 10m? (pros/cons list in full runbook).
- Confirm on-call rotations for the weekend run (Priya cannot cover after 10pm).

References & bookmarks:
- Jira: PROJ-1983 (rollout ticket)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/421
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/rollout-runbook
- Slack thread: #release-ops (pin message id: 7842)

Quick personal checklist (notes to Maya):
- Print paper copy of this doc for the ops desk.
- Bring laptop with local dashboard snapshots (esp. error-rate panel).
- Remind customer success to hold pre-emptive email template ready.

-- end of quickref --

(Informal fragments below — do not publish directly)
- fragment: "if sampler sees any model drift, drop to 25% and re-eval prompt set A."
- fragment: "consider enabling traffic soft-throttle instead of hard pause; lowers oscillation risk."
